evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Kishida ordered an investigation into the Unification Church after the assassination of Shinzo Abe exposed close ties between the church and ruling-party lawmakers, and that the government would clarify the situation and expand relief for victims.

evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Kishida ordered an investigation into the Unification Church after the assassination of Shinzo Abe exposed close ties between the church and ruling-party lawmakers, and that the government would clarify the situation and expand relief for victims.
evidence.source_locator: lead paragraph and early body text
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent wire reporting on a concrete ruler-directed probe, with the main limitation that the article is syndicated through Investing.com rather than Reuters' own page.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct: Kishida ordered the investigation and framed the relief response.
contrary_evidence: The probe was reactive and followed public scandal, so it shows correction more than clean prior restraint.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that economic revitalization minister Daishiro Yamagiwa stepped down after criticism that he failed to fully explain his Unification Church ties; Kishida said he accepted the resignation, felt responsible for appointing him, and would name a successor.
evidence.title: Japanese economic minister steps down over church links
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that economic revitalization minister Daishiro Yamagiwa stepped down after criticism that he failed to fully explain his Unification Church ties; Kishida said he accepted the resignation, felt responsible for appointing him, and would name a successor.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent wire reporting on a resignation directly affecting Kishida's administration and on Kishida's own statement that he felt responsible; the article is syndicated and focused on political fallout rather than personal corruption evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material: the appointment and retention decisions are Kishida's, though the underlying church links belong to the minister.
contrary_evidence: The minister's own conduct is not Kishida's own dishonesty; this is vetting and oversight evidence rather than proof of personal self-dealing.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that internal affairs minister Minoru Terada resigned over a funding scandal, becoming the third cabinet member to leave in less than a month, and that Terada had been under fire for several funding scandals.
evidence.title: Third Japanese cabinet minister in a month resigns in blow to PM
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that internal affairs minister Minoru Terada resigned over a funding scandal, becoming the third cabinet member to leave in less than a month, and that Terada had been under fire for several funding scandals.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting on a resignation from Kishida's cabinet and the reason for it; it is good evidence of appointment/retention problems but not of Kishida's personal financial misconduct.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but meaningful through Kishida's appointment and retention of the minister; the scandal itself is the minister's.
contrary_evidence: The source does not attribute the funding scandal to Kishida personally.

evidence.claim: Kyodo reported that ruling-party lawmaker Kentaro Sonoura would resign over a political funds scandal and noted that three Cabinet members had already been effectively sacked over various scandals in recent months.
evidence.title: Japan ruling party lawmaker to resign over political funds scandal
evidence.excerpt: Kyodo reported that ruling-party lawmaker Kentaro Sonoura would resign over a political funds scandal and noted that three Cabinet members had already been effectively sacked over various scandals in recent months.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous independent reporting with specific legal/factual detail about the scandal and the broader cabinet fallout; it still concerns Kishida's network rather than Kishida's own finances.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant because the scandal sits inside Kishida's ruling network and administration; it does not prove his own misconduct.
contrary_evidence: The article is about another lawmaker, not Kishida personally.

evidence.claim: Kishida said he met directly with people harmed by the former Unification Church, instructed a new law to be drafted and enacted during the Diet session, and coordinated ruling and opposition parties so the relief system would work reliably.
evidence.title: Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida
evidence.excerpt: Kishida said he met directly with people harmed by the former Unification Church, instructed a new law to be drafted and enacted during the Diet session, and coordinated ruling and opposition parties so the relief system would work reliably.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official transcript describing concrete corrective action, victim contact, and inter-party coordination; the main limitation is that it is Kishida's own account of his response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct: Kishida personally described the meetings and issued the drafting instruction.
contrary_evidence: This was a reactive remedy after public scandal and visible harm, not evidence that the underlying conduct had been absent.

evidence.claim: Kishida said the FY2022 supplementary budget of 2.7 trillion yen had been approved and enacted, and that it supported household finances, gasoline-price caps, regional grants, SME cost pass-through, and temporary employment measures.
evidence.title: Press Conference by the Prime Minister on the Approval of the FY2022 Supplementary Budget and Other Matters
evidence.excerpt: Kishida said the FY2022 supplementary budget of 2.7 trillion yen had been approved and enacted, and that it supported household finances, gasoline-price caps, regional grants, SME cost pass-through, and temporary employment measures.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official transcript with concrete budget and implementation details from the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Kishida as the prime minister announcing and defending the budget package.
contrary_evidence: The package was reactive to external shocks, so it shows execution under pressure rather than autonomous growth creation.

evidence.claim: Kishida held the ninth meeting of the Digital Garden City council and the participants discussed a comprehensive strategy formulation policy for the initiative.
evidence.title: Council for the Realization of the Vision for a Digital Garden City Nation
evidence.excerpt: Kishida held the ninth meeting of the Digital Garden City council and the participants discussed a comprehensive strategy formulation policy for the initiative.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official record of a concrete coordinating meeting, though it shows planning more than completed delivery.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Kishida as the chairing prime minister.
contrary_evidence: This is a planning/coordination artifact, not evidence that the full regional program had already delivered outcomes.

evidence.claim: Kishida said women's economic independence was core to the new form of capitalism and tied it to closing the gender wage gap through mandatory disclosure by large companies.
evidence.title: Opening Remarks by Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio at the World Assembly for Women: WAW! 2022
evidence.excerpt: Kishida said women's economic independence was core to the new form of capitalism and tied it to closing the gender wage gap through mandatory disclosure by large companies.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official speech with explicit policy framing and a concrete regulatory mechanism.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly Kishida's own program articulation and policy direction.
contrary_evidence: The speech states goals and mechanisms, not proven labor-market results by year-end 2022.

evidence.claim: Kishida said the Diet session passed almost all government bills, including the second FY2022 supplementary budget and the Infectious Diseases Control Law amendment, and that the cabinet would deliver energy assistance, child-rearing support, and a higher childbirth allowance.
evidence.title: Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida
evidence.excerpt: Kishida said the Diet session passed almost all government bills, including the second FY2022 supplementary budget and the Infectious Diseases Control Law amendment, and that the cabinet would deliver energy assistance, child-rearing support, and a higher childbirth allowance.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official transcript showing legislative completion and concrete implementation measures.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Kishida as prime minister and party leader driving the package.
contrary_evidence: The measures were compensatory responses to inflation and family-cost pressures, not evidence that those pressures had been eliminated.

evidence.claim: The cabinet approved the new National Security Strategy, National Defense Strategy, and Defense Buildup Program; Kishida said he had advanced the review through 18 National Security Council meetings and set a 43 trillion yen defense buildup with stable funding.
evidence.title: Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida
evidence.excerpt: The cabinet approved the new National Security Strategy, National Defense Strategy, and Defense Buildup Program; Kishida said he had advanced the review through 18 National Security Council meetings and set a 43 trillion yen defense buildup with stable funding.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official record of a major strategic decision, the coordination process behind it, and the funding framework.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Kishida's chairmanship and repeated coordination of the security-policy process.
contrary_evidence: This is strong on mobilization and budgeting, but it does not by itself prove effective long-run strategic outcomes.

evidence.claim: MHLW said the women’s active participation rules were amended and that large employers with 301 or more regular employees must disclose gender wage-gap information.
evidence.title: 2022年7月8日より、従業員が301人以上の企業は「男女の賃金の差異」の情報公表が義務化されました
evidence.excerpt: MHLW said the women’s active participation rules were amended and that large employers with 301 or more regular employees must disclose gender wage-gap information.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry notice giving the legal change, effective date, and coverage threshold.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but meaningful as a Kishida-administration regulatory change tied to the new capitalism agenda.
contrary_evidence: The notice shows a disclosure rule, not the eventual labor-market impact of that rule.

evidence.claim: The June 2022 Child Welfare Act revision strengthened comprehensive support for at-risk children and families, added municipal duties for planned support, and made child-family centers an effort obligation.
evidence.title: 令和4年６月に成立した改正児童福祉法について
evidence.excerpt: The June 2022 Child Welfare Act revision strengthened comprehensive support for at-risk children and families, added municipal duties for planned support, and made child-family centers an effort obligation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry explanation of enacted reform and its substantive content.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Kishida's cabinet because the reform was enacted and later operationalized under his administration.
contrary_evidence: The same page says child abuse deaths had not ceased and consultation cases remained above 200,000, showing the problem was still severe.

evidence.claim: From October 1, 2022, both parents could split childcare leave into two separate periods, expanding practical leave options.
evidence.title: 育児休業｜育児休業制度特設サイト
evidence.excerpt: From October 1, 2022, both parents could split childcare leave into two separate periods, expanding practical leave options.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry policy page describing the rule change and effective date, though the page itself is not framed as a dated news release.
evidence.period_fit: The implementation date is within the 2022 target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but meaningful; it reflects nationwide policy implementation by Kishida's government.
contrary_evidence: The page does not show take-up rates or whether the change reached all eligible workers equally.

evidence.claim: The IMF said Japan was recovering under strong policy support but still needed deep reforms to raise productivity and achieve inclusive, sustainable growth.
evidence.title: Japan: 2022 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Japan
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said Japan was recovering under strong policy support but still needed deep reforms to raise productivity and achieve inclusive, sustainable growth.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Authoritative country surveillance from the IMF, useful for outcome and constraint context rather than just government self-report.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable: the report reflects Kishida-era policy support, but it also stresses inherited structural limits and pandemic recovery effects.
contrary_evidence: The IMF explicitly says deep reforms were still needed, which limits credit for completed effectiveness by year-end 2022.

evidence.claim: The OECD estimated that household purchasing power in Japan fell 3 percent between August 2021 and August 2022, with low-income and rural households hit especially hard.
evidence.title: A cost-of-living squeeze? Distributional implications of rising inflation
evidence.excerpt: The OECD estimated that household purchasing power in Japan fell 3 percent between August 2021 and August 2022, with low-income and rural households hit especially hard.
evidence.source_locator: main body text around the Japan estimate
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent cross-country OECD analysis using household budget and CPI data; strong for distributional outcomes.
evidence.period_fit: The estimated period straddles the target year and directly covers 2022 conditions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable: the inflation shock was external, but the government response and targeting choices were Kishida's.
contrary_evidence: The OECD analysis is not a direct evaluation of Kishida's policy design, only of household impact.

evidence.claim: For 2022, workers' household monthly income rose 2.0 percent nominally but fell 1.0 percent in real terms, while consumption also lagged inflation in real terms.
evidence.title: Statistics Bureau Home Page/News Bulletin February 28, 2023
evidence.excerpt: For 2022, workers' household monthly income rose 2.0 percent nominally but fell 1.0 percent in real terms, while consumption also lagged inflation in real terms.
evidence.source_locator: Family Income and Expenditure Survey section, 2022 Yearly Average
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official national statistics release with the relevant yearly-average household series.
evidence.period_fit: The data summarize the target year 2022, published shortly after year-end.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable: these are household outcomes under Kishida's 2022 policy environment, but they also reflect external inflation shocks.
contrary_evidence: Positive nominal income growth does not offset the real-income decline.

evidence.claim: Kishida said the government had finalized the Grand Design and Action Plan for a New Form of Capitalism and would implement concrete multi-year plans for startups, green transformation, and measures to double asset income.
evidence.title: Joint Meeting of the Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy and the Council of New Form of Capitalism Realization
evidence.excerpt: Kishida said the government had finalized the Grand Design and Action Plan for a New Form of Capitalism and would implement concrete multi-year plans for startups, green transformation, and measures to double asset income.
evidence.source_locator: lines 39-51, Prime Minister's remarks after the joint meeting
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary PMO transcript with explicit policy-finalization language and implementation commitments.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022, at the point the policy package was finalized.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Kishida as prime minister chairing and announcing the package; execution still depended on the cabinet and line ministries.
contrary_evidence: This is a commitment and design document, not evidence of delivery by itself.
Later outcome data still show mixed results under inflation pressure.

evidence.claim: The government says it decided the Startup Development Five-year Plan on November 28, 2022 and will push the three pillars of human capital and network building, funding and exit diversification, and open innovation as one package.
evidence.title: Startup Development Portal Site
evidence.excerpt: The government says it decided the Startup Development Five-year Plan on November 28, 2022 and will push the three pillars of human capital and network building, funding and exit diversification, and open innovation as one package.
evidence.source_locator: intro paragraph on the portal landing page
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Cabinet Secretariat portal explicitly states the decision date, the plan name, and the policy pillars.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to the Kishida cabinet's policy timetable.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Kishida's cabinet agenda; downstream execution still depended on agencies, firms, and local implementers.
contrary_evidence: The portal describes intended execution rather than measured outcomes.
Startup targets are ambitious and do not by themselves show success.

evidence.claim: In FY2022 the JFTC opened 116 antimonopoly investigations and took 11 legal measures, including eight cease-and-desist orders and three commitment plan approvals.
evidence.title: FY2022 (April 2022-March 2023) Annual Report
evidence.excerpt: In FY2022 the JFTC opened 116 antimonopoly investigations and took 11 legal measures, including eight cease-and-desist orders and three commitment plan approvals.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary regulator annual report with quantified enforcement statistics for the relevant fiscal year.
evidence.period_fit: Covers FY2022, overlapping the 2022 ruler period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material: the JFTC is an independent regulator, yet its enforcement and advocacy posture reflects the government framework Kishida was using.
contrary_evidence: This shows institutional enforcement capacity more than direct personal direction from Kishida.
It does not isolate which cases, if any, were uniquely Kishida-driven.

evidence.claim: The JFTC established the Office of Economic Analysis on April 1, 2022 to strengthen high-quality economic analysis for antimonopoly enforcement and competition-policy planning.
evidence.title: FY2022 (April 2022-March 2023) Annual Report
evidence.excerpt: The JFTC established the Office of Economic Analysis on April 1, 2022 to strengthen high-quality economic analysis for antimonopoly enforcement and competition-policy planning.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary regulator annual report explicitly states the institutional change and its purpose.
evidence.period_fit: Within FY2022 and squarely within the 2022 period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect: this is a regulator-institution change, not a personal action uniquely owned by Kishida, but it fits the cabinet's competition-policy framework.
contrary_evidence: The report does not prove Kishida personally directed the office's work.
Institutional strengthening does not by itself show reduced capture or favoritism.

evidence.claim: The June 2023 follow-up said that in the year since the June 2022 cabinet decision the government had concretely advanced the Startup Development Five-year Plan, the Asset Income Doubling Plan, and integrated labor-market reforms.
evidence.title: Follow-up on the Grand Design and Action Plan for a New Form of Capitalism
evidence.excerpt: The June 2023 follow-up said that in the year since the June 2022 cabinet decision the government had concretely advanced the Startup Development Five-year Plan, the Asset Income Doubling Plan, and integrated labor-market reforms.
evidence.source_locator: lines 16-19 of the ministerial press-conference summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official follow-up summary, strong for what the government says it advanced, but still self-reported and not independently audited in the page itself.
evidence.period_fit: Cross-period follow-up on the 2022 package; useful for implementation tracking with one-year lag.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but meaningful: this is the cabinet office summarizing Kishida-era policy execution, though results also reflect private-sector and macroeconomic conditions.
contrary_evidence: This is a government self-assessment, not an independent evaluation.
It does not separately measure implementation quality across ministries.

evidence.claim: The June 2023 follow-up said private-sector wage increases had reached a 30-year high and that high investment appetite had begun to emerge.
evidence.title: Follow-up on the Grand Design and Action Plan for a New Form of Capitalism
evidence.excerpt: The June 2023 follow-up said private-sector wage increases had reached a 30-year high and that high investment appetite had begun to emerge.
evidence.source_locator: lines 17-18 of the ministerial press-conference summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official follow-up summary with an outcome statement, but still self-reported and not a substitute for independent labor-market microdata.
evidence.period_fit: Cross-period follow-up on the 2022 policy package; useful for judging early directional progress.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable: the cabinet's wage-push and investment agenda likely helped, but external inflation and reopening effects also mattered.
contrary_evidence: The statement mixes policy progress with broader macro conditions.
It does not isolate Kishida's causal effect from business-cycle recovery.
